questions.q: What does Query Profile show for a single query?
options: A visual execution plan of operator nodes, each showing its percentage of total query time
A list of every query that has ever run in the account
The dollar cost of running that specific query
The role and warehouse used, with no execution detail
questions.explain: Query Profile is a graph of the operator nodes Snowflake actually executed for one query, wired together with arrows showing row counts, each annotated with its share of total time.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the single most useful number when reading a Query Profile?
options: Each operator node's percentage of total query time
The total number of columns in the source table
The account's current credit balance
The number of users currently logged in
questions.explain: The time-percentage on each node tells you exactly which step is worth investigating, rather than guessing across a query with many operators.

questions.q: What does it mean when a Join operator's output row count is dramatically larger than either of its inputs?
options: It likely signals an unintended cross join or a join key that isn't as selective as assumed
It means the query ran perfectly with no issues
It means the warehouse was oversized for the query
It means the result was served entirely from the result cache
questions.explain: An 'exploding join' — output much bigger than either input — is a classic sign of an unintended cross join or a poorly selective join key, and is one of the things this lesson says to look for.

questions.q: What does Query History show that Query Profile does not?
options: Every query that ran, so you can find the slow ones in the first place
The exact operator-node breakdown of one specific query
Row-level data from the queried tables
The masking policy attached to a column
questions.explain: Query Profile drills into one query's execution plan; Query History lists every query that ran (via the Snowsight page or QUERY_HISTORY() in SQL) so you can identify which ones were slow.

questions.q: What does it mean when an operator node in Query Profile 'spilled' to local or remote disk?
options: The warehouse ran out of memory for that operator and wrote intermediate results to disk
The query returned zero rows
The table's data was physically moved to a different disk
The query was automatically cancelled
questions.explain: Spilling happens when a node runs out of memory on the assigned warehouse and writes intermediate results to disk — a strong signal the warehouse may be undersized for that query.
